I farm 10.1 mu in Quzhou County, and this year I will keep the whole area in cotton because that is the crop I know best and it fits my land and irrigation conditions. Since some people in my household work off-farm, I will keep the plan steady and manageable rather than making it too labor-intensive. I have ten years of experience, so I would rather rely on a familiar cotton schedule with improved seed, moderate fertilizer, several key irrigations from the well, and regular pest control. At the start of the season, I will prepare the land with rotary tillage because it is efficient for my scale and helps me get a clean seedbed. For fertilizer, I will not push too hard; I will use a moderate rate of nitrogen with balanced phosphorus and potassium so the crop grows steadily without excessive vegetative growth. Because I have well irrigation, I will plan several irrigations at the main water-demand stages. Cotton usually needs careful insect management, so I will spray several times across the season depending on pressure. With this approach, I am aiming for a stable yield rather than taking big risks.
